caption: I costed the vet plan and the food before I got him. Nobody warned me about the couch. What did your pet actually end up costing?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R33 000
p/m salary
Living in Hermanus
slides.body:
Male, 29
Single, no kids
Job: Junior architect
Net salary: R33 000 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 1 bed in town, small garden for the dog
slides.body: Paid R1 200 more than the flat without a garden. Worth it, mostly for him.

slides.title: Dog costs
slides.includes: Food, vet plan, the couch he's slowly destroying
slides.body: I costed the food and the vet care before I got him. I did not cost the couch.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: Bought for site visits. Now mostly used to drive the dog to the beach.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Woolworths mostly, the occasional big Spar shop
slides.body: Cooking for one, still buying like there might be guests.

slides.title: Eating out & coffee
slides.body: I guessed R900. It's R2 100. Hermanus makes it very easy to eat out.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol & insurance, medical aid, phone & fibre, funeral policy, gym, savings, professional body fees
slides.body: R12 550 of things I've never once looked at as a group. That's more than a third of what I earn.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R33 000. On paper that's a comfortable salary for one person. A dog and a Hermanus postcode use up more of it than either should.

slides.title: I stopped guessing what he actually cost me
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The couch didn't show up as a line item, but the vet visits after did.

No bank login needed.
